title: Decide profileSnapshotVersion at the first release
description: The WCLI-10 review found a commitment with no gate behind it. domain/profile.ts holds profileSnapshotVersion at 1, with a written rule saying it must be bumped in the same change that alters what normalizeProfile accepts, and a written exception saying it stays 1 while the accepted set is still being settled because no released build has written a snapshot yet. WCLI-10 narrowed the accepted set and did not bump, correctly, because the narrowing can only refuse more and so fails closed. That reasoning expires the moment a release writes snapshots: from then on a stored record outlives the rules that wrote it, and the version is what stops a later build reading it as an approval the developer gave. The obligation currently lives only in a source comment, which is not read by whoever cuts the release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The release that first ships to a user carries a written profileSnapshotVersion decision: either a bump with the comment above the constant updated, or the reason it still does not require one.
The decision is reachable from the release gate rather than from a source comment alone, so whoever cuts the release meets it without rediscovering this record.

implementationNotes: CLOSED 2026-09-29 (this pull request). DEC-50 recorded as ADR 0018: profileSnapshotVersion stays 1 while Ward is unreleased and the release commit bumps it, refusing dev-era snapshots with no migration. The obligation is step 1 of the new release runbook (docs/runbooks/cutting-a-ward-release.md), which also gathers the other recorded release-time obligations, and WCLI-15 now carries a note pointing at it; the comment above the constant names both. AC0 is checked on the pre-release reading: the written decision and the updated comment are what can exist before a release, and the bump itself is a gated release step. finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/ward-cli#129.
